evidence.title: Lanes Desktop
evidence.finding: Issues own sessions and worktrees; model gateway supports user-hosted endpoints.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop MCP
evidence.finding: Local research-preview MCP reads/edits the board and controls sessions.

evidence.title: Dependencies
evidence.finding: Blocked issues are skipped by automatic pickup; humans can override board placement.

evidence.title: Collaboration
evidence.finding: Shared board and roles documented; active sessions lock issue takeover.

evidence.title: Lanes pricing
evidence.finding: Desktop included; Pro collaboration, while remote workspaces also marked coming soon.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop
evidence.locator: What platforms does Lanes run on?
evidence.finding: Desktop FAQ says macOS runs today and other platforms are on the roadmap.

evidence.title: Lanes Issue board
evidence.finding: Issues have title, description, instructions, CLI and worktree settings. Board statuses are customizable; issue edits auto-save; label/project/worktree filtering and bulk actions exist.

evidence.title: Lanes Sessions
evidence.locator: Many sessions per issue; settings; history; controls
evidence.finding: Multiple named PTY sessions share an issue worktree with separate transcripts, tokens/cost/runtime metrics and lifecycle state. Claude sessions resume history; users stop/steer through terminals.

evidence.title: Lanes Dependencies
evidence.finding: Dependencies reject cycles and skip blocked issues during queue auto-pickup. Humans can manually move blocked issues; prerequisites reaching Done unblock dependents.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop MCP
evidence.locator: Enabling; Issues; Sessions; History; external trackers
evidence.finding: Opt-in research-preview local SSE server lets agents create/read/edit/move issues, start/stop/resume sessions, read history/statistics/terminal output and bridge GitHub/Linear.

evidence.title: Lanes Harness selection
evidence.finding: Claude Code and Codex are first-class; others run as plain shell sessions. Detects installed versions and offers install/update.

evidence.title: Lanes Model gateway
evidence.finding: Gateway changes provider through session environment, chiefly Claude Code Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Supports Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM and token providers; Codex file config is not driven by environment mappings.

evidence.title: Lanes Worktree management
evidence.finding: Issue worktrees have separate branches/directories. Sibling sessions share one issue worktree. User scripts run tests; complete-and-merge commits/merges and cleans up with dirty-work warnings.

evidence.title: Lanes Git changes
evidence.finding: Monaco inline diff and commit history are available. Commits stage everything; no hunk staging, side-by-side diff or conflict-resolution UI. Uncommit/discard applies only to latest unpushed commit.

evidence.title: Lanes GitHub integration
evidence.finding: Imports external issues with source URL, refreshes title/body after overwrite warning, and supports write-back comments. PR creation uses local gh within a session; no PR MCP tool.

evidence.title: Lanes Linear integration
evidence.finding: Imports Linear title/body/state/URL; MCP reads/creates/comments on tickets. Projects/cycles/priority are not mapped and state mapping is not automatic.

evidence.title: Lanes Settings
evidence.finding: Project JSON controls quick commands, labels, CLI flags and base branch. PR opening moves issue to Review; Done may stop sessions. Folder-access checks and launch flags are documented.

evidence.title: Lanes Agent loops
evidence.locator: Before you start; scheduled and fan-out examples; brakes
evidence.finding: External agents drive MCP to start/check sessions and advance issues. Examples use harness loop/schedules; desktop must stay running. Verification and bounded retries/time are workflow guidance.

evidence.title: Lanes Collaboration
evidence.finding: Remote synced workspaces document Admin/Editor permissions, workspace chat/presence and shared board. Active issues lock takeover; AI takeover starts fresh and clears terminal history. Pricing availability conflicts remain.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop overview
evidence.finding: macOS Ventura+ native Intel/Apple Silicon app. Other platforms are on the roadmap. Existing CLI login/API keys are reused; code/prompts/terminal data stay local.

evidence.title: Lanes pricing
evidence.finding: Free forever one-user plan; Pro $19/month up to ten members. Desktop included on every plan. Remote workspaces, Slack and automations are labeled Coming soon.

evidence.title: Lanes repository README
evidence.finding: Desktop uses Tauri 2/React/Rust/SQLite; local issues/settings stay in SQLite. Crash reporting is on by default with Settings > User > General opt-out. License section says Proprietary, all rights reserved.

evidence.title: Lanes v0.50.0
evidence.finding: Released 2026-10-31 with custom statuses and a setting controlling stop-on-Done.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop Quick start
evidence.locator: 1. Install; 2. Point Lanes at your code; 3. Create an issue; 4. Start a session
evidence.finding: Homebrew install, Add a project, Cmd+N creates a draft Backlog issue with Instructions, then Plan or Implement starts a session.

evidence.title: Lanes Labels & Filtering
evidence.locator: Assigning labels; Filtering by labels; Filtering by working directory; Filtering by workflow step
evidence.finding: Per-repository labels can be assigned to issues; the board filters by label, working directory and workflow step, with sort controls.

evidence.title: Lanes Privacy Policy
evidence.locator: 1. Information We Collect: Analytics and Telemetry Data; 4. How We Use Your Information; 5. Third-Party Services
evidence.finding: Policy covering the Lanes desktop application discloses anonymous telemetry (feature-usage events, health pings, session duration, app version, OS, crash reports) via Google Analytics 4/Firebase and Sentry. It names no telemetry opt-out control.

evidence.title: Lanes Desktop MCP
evidence.locator: Introduction; Settings > Integrations > Lanes MCP; Sessions
evidence.finding: Lanes Desktop MCP is a research preview enabled under Settings > Integrations > Lanes MCP, with one-click connection for supported agents. Its tools start Claude Code, Codex or shell sessions against issues, stop and resume them, check status across running sessions and pull session message history.
